jobs.title: Program Director, Innovation Fund
jobs.description:
The California Health Care Foundation (CHCF) is a nonprofit, nonpartisan philanthropy dedicated to advancing meaningful, measurable improvements in the way the health care delivery system serves all Californians — with a particular focus on those with low incomes and those whose needs are not well met by the status quo. CHCF deploys approximately $40 million per year across grants and investments, working at the intersection of health policy, innovation, and equity to strengthen California's safety net.

Central to CHCF's work is its Health Innovation Fund, a program-related investment vehicle that deploys venture capital into the Medicaid and safety net ecosystem. CHCF invests strategically — bringing mission alignment, deep sector knowledge, and a powerful network as its primary value-add to portfolio companies and co-investors alike.

Position Description

The Director, Innovation Fund is one of five program directors at CHCF and a member of the senior management team, reporting to the Senior Vice President of Strategy and Programs. This is a meaningful leadership role, impacting the entire Foundation: the Director leads both the foundation's venture investing activity (Series A/B, Medicaid-focused) and its grantmaking in AI and technology — deploying approximately $1M in investment capital and up to $500K in grant capital per deal, with 2–3 new investments per year. The Director also contributes to meaningful foundation-wide initiatives outside of their day-to-day managing the Fund.

The Director leads a small, high-performing team, staffs an Innovation Fund advisor group of 6–7 VC investors and a board liaison, and holds board observer seats at portfolio companies. CHCF's expectation is that the right candidate will grow into this role for the long term and help shape the future of their organization.

Candidate Responsibilities

Serve as a member of CHCF’s senior management team, contributing to organization-wide leadership, culture, and operational initiatives
Lead the strategy, sourcing, due diligence, and ongoing management of the CHCF Health Innovation Fund's portfolio of program-related investments, primarily Series A/B companies serving Medicaid and safety net populations
Oversee a complementary grantmaking portfolio focused on AI and technology innovation in health care, developing funding recommendations and work plans aligned with CHCF's mission and budget
Hold board observer seats at portfolio companies and serve as a credible, mission-driven voice in syndicate relationships with co-investors and health care venture funds
Staff and manage the Innovation Fund advisor group (6–7 external VC investors + board liaison), including preparation for biannual meetings and ongoing relationship management
Provide leadership, mentorship, and accountability to program staff, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team environment
Represent CHCF externally with health care leaders, policymakers, philanthropic partners, and the broader investment community — at conferences, convenings, and in the field (~6 trips/year, primarily within California)
Collaborate cross-functionally with communications, finance, grants administration, and legal teams to ensure effective program execution, reporting, and dissemination of insights

Candidate Qualifications

Demonstrated investing experience, ideally at the Series A/B stage in health tech or Medicaid-adjacent sectors; credibility to step into board observer seats on day one is essential
Mission alignment with Medicaid, safety net health care, and health equity — genuine curiosity about the sector is required; deep Medicaid expertise is not required on day one, but must be a sincere area of interest
People leadership experience; this role manages a team and requires authentic management capability — candidates who have not yet led teams should be prepared to speak concretely to how they've developed others
Advanced degree in public health, health care administration, public policy, or a related field; MD, PhD, or equivalent clinical/research degree preferred, or equivalent professional experience
At least 10 years of experience leading complex initiatives in health care, health policy, venture investing, impact investing, or a related field, including substantial experience in strategic planning and organizational leadership
Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex investment and programmatic decisions for diverse audiences, including board members, grantees, and community stakeholders
Commitment to anti-racist principles and active participation in diversity, equity, and inclusion efforts, consistent with CHCF's organizational values and culture

CHCF is partnering with Oxeon to fill this position. Interested candidates should contact Sonia Millsom (sonia@oxeon.com) or Sofia Hubbard (sofia@oxeon.com) to express interest.

Company Description

Unitek Learning is a leading healthcare education organization focused on preparing the next generation of nurses and healthcare professionals.

Through its family of institutions, including Unitek College of Nursing, Eagle Gate College, Provo College, Brookline College, and Unitek EMT, Unitek delivers career-focused education designed to help students build meaningful careers while addressing critical workforce needs across the healthcare industry.

Through our Workforce Solutions segment, Unitek partners with hospitals and health systems to create sustainable talent pipelines and expand access to healthcare education through employer-based training and workforce development programs nationwide.

Are you an experienced Medical Assistant ready to step into leadership and make a lasting impact? We’re seeking a Program Director – Medical Assisting to lead the planning, development, and daily operations of our program while supporting student success and academic excellence. Description

Duties Description

The Sr. Director of Operations serves as the head of the Division’s administrative services and its financial and operational systems. The selected candidate will be charged with the oversight and administration of the Division’s personnel, fiscal, and training units. This role ensures that the Division has the necessary resources, processes, and personnel to effectively certify MWBEs, advocate for their utilization in State contracting, and maintain compliance with Article 15-A of Executive Law.

Duties Include But Are Not Limited To

Administer DMWBD’s entire operations support program.
In collaboration with the EVP of the Division, oversee the Division’s strategic planning, development, and implementation of work programs, priorities, scheduling/coordination of major projects and activities with other divisions, bureaus, and State agencies.
Manage all Division funding and contracts.
In collaboration with the Executive Director, work with the Executive Chamber and ESD Finance to manage the Division’s annual budget, track expenditures, and forecast the Division’s future financial needs.
Oversee the lifecycle of Division contracts, including third-party vendors providing technical assistance or IT support for the MWBE certification system.
Serve as the liaison between the DMWBD and ESD’s Division of Administration.
Assist in developing management plans to measure the performance of subordinate areas of operation; identify strengths and weaknesses in existing procedures; assist in the development and implementation of new and improved procedures.
Coordinate the activities of subordinate staff to ensure that policies, procedures, and standards are applied consistently, and that management and administrative practices of the operational sections are handled in accordance with the policies established by the EVP.
Direct the operational onboarding of new staff and coordinate with section supervisors to ensure that office resource allocations align with evolving departmental priorities.
Coordinate and participate in training activities, ensuring that necessary training is identified and available, and coordinate employee nomination and attendance.
Provide managerial support to section supervisors and provide guidance, as needed.
Represent the Division in meetings with other agencies, vendors, and stakeholders.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Education Requirements: A bachelor’s degree in business administration, public administration, finance, or a related field. A master’s degree (MBA or MPA) is highly preferred.

Professional Experience Requirements: A minimum of five (5) years of progressive experience in operations management, public administration, or procurement.

At least two (2) years in a senior leadership or supervisory capacity within a government agency or a large, complex organization.
Proven experience managing departmental budgets and overseeing high-volume procurement/requisition processes.

Substitutions

A master’s degree may substitute for one year of specialized experience.
A Ph.D. may substitute for two years of specialized experience.

Knowledge Requirements

In-depth understanding of New York State procurement laws and Article 15-A.
Strong familiarity with the Statewide Financial System (SFS) or similar enterprise resource planning (ERP) software.
Exceptional organizational, analytical, and communication skills.

SALARY RANGE: $103,870 - $131,298

ABOUT CLASS ACTION

Class Action is a student-driven nonprofit holding elite colleges accountable to their public missions. Our work has been featured in The Guardian , The New York Times , Wall Street Journal , Forbes , TIME , and other major outlets.

“Elite” institutions are failing the public. They admit more students from the top 1% than the bottom 50% combined, accumulate massive endowments to serve a vanishingly small number of students, and push the majority of graduates into finance, consulting, and tech. All while taking billions in public funding.

In just two years, we’ve built a movement using community organizing methods to challenge them to do better. With student-led chapters on campuses across the country, we played a pivotal role in passing legislation aimed at ending legacy admissions in California, hosted conferences at Brown and Yale Universities, launched a widely-cited research hub, and reframed the debate about elite higher education. Now, we're expanding our team.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The debate over the purpose of elite higher education, and whether it will serve the public or continue to entrench privilege, is at a fever pitch. You’ll help students win it.

You'll build and run our communications program across social and traditional media, working directly with students to turn their campaigns into viral videos, posts and stories. That means shaping how the country talks about admissions and access, endowment hoarding, the pipelines that funnel graduates into finance, consulting, and Big Tech, and more. You'll train students to amplify their messages, place op-eds and stories with national reporters, and grow our social media audience. 

Two big projects are on the horizon. The first is a Truth Campaign-style effort to change how students see corporate recruiting. Top firms spend millions on campus recruiting infrastructure built to make their jobs feel urgent, inevitable, and prestigious. Our job is to make that machinery visible and move the campus conversation from "you're selling out" to "you're being funneled by your university and corporations." The second is our third annual conference, where roughly 200 organizers from 25 campuses will gather at Harvard in October to ratify a national platform for reforming elite higher education. With a five-figure budget and a team of student organizers, your goal will be to make the country hear about it.

RAD Creative Campus (comprehensive fundraising )

Develop annual and multi-year development plans with goals, strategies, timelines, and performance indicators.
Build development operations and systems: CRM/data integrity, gift processing/acknowledgment, moves management, reporting, stewardship practices, and tool/technology recommendations.
Assist with fundraising events in collaboration with the Executive Director

·      Serve as the primary internal partner to our external campaign council consultant team to maintain momentum, coordinate prospect development, prepare materials, and embed durable systems and capacity beyond the campaign.

Significant experience in nonprofit development (institutional giving, major gifts, and/or capital/comprehensive campaigns). Experience within arts and culture, community/economic development, workforce development, or a related field is particularly relevant.
Demonstrated success developing fundraising strategy and securing significant philanthropic support.
Strong grants experience, including reporting and compliance.
Campaign experience preferred (seven-figure goals and above).
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to translate complex vision into compelling philanthropic opportunities.
Strong project management; able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Experience with donor databases/CRMs and development reporting.
High integrity, sound judgment, and discretion with confidential information.
Entrepreneurial, collaborative, and comfortable building systems in a growing organization.

Relationship builder grounded in trust, shared purpose, and long-term engagement.
Strategic and detail-oriented—able to set direction and execute.
Brings structure and accountability without dampening creativity and collaboration.
Understands the Foundation’s priorities—capacity building, programs, artist investment, district recovery/evolution, and the capital initiative—as an interconnected story for funders.

Measures of Success (first 12-18 months)

Launch and execute a multi-year development strategy aligned to annual needs and the Creative Campus campaign.
Build and manage a qualified fundraising pipeline across campaign, institutional, major gifts, corporate, and public funding.
Advance the Creative Campus campaign toward the approximately $20M goal in partnership with leadership and DeVos Institute.

Increase flexible/unrestricted revenue.
Strengthen Board and leadership fundraising participation.
Expand the Foundation’s philanthropic network locally, regionally, and nationally.

Longer-term success includes dollars raised and the creation of a diversified, sustainable development program that supports both RADA Foundation and the RAD Creative Campus well beyond the campaign.

Our core petitions platform, used by more than 100 million people annually, is growing rapidly - and we are rebuilding it from the ground-up using new tools to turn anyone into a powerful civic leader on the issues they care about. Soon we will launch a new platform to identify the >80% of issues that most people agree on, locally and nationally, and to mobilize hundreds of millions of people to advocate for those common-ground solutions.

To realize this vision, we’re expanding the most talented team in the world at the intersection of technology and social impact - all focused every day on building healthier democracies globally.

Own end-to-end delivery of civic dialogues, holding a biweekly launch cadence at high quality across all active cities, from recruitment through facilitation to post-dialogue reporting.
Lead and grow the program manager team, hiring and onboarding PMs as the program scales and developing them into confident, independent operators.
Redesign and document the 12-week dialogue playbook into a repeatable system with AI-powered workflows (participant matching, synthesis, insight extraction) that scale across cities.

People and team leadership: Leading, hiring, and developing a distributed team of experienced program managers, often in ambiguous, early-stage conditions.
